import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points

Do algebraic curves of genus $g \geq 2$ over number fields $K$ have at most some bounded
number $N(K, g)$ of $K$-rational points?

Following the literature (e.g. [DGH2021]), a curve over $K$ is a smooth, projective,
geometrically irreducible variety of dimension $1$ over $K$. We model it as a scheme `C` with a
structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K` that is proper and smooth of relative dimension `1`, whose
base change to an algebraic closure of `K` is irreducible. The genus of `C` is
$\dim_K H^0(C, \Omega^1_{C/K})$, the dimension of the space of global regular differentials; we
compute it inside the function field $K(C)$ as the space of Kähler differentials of $K(C)/K$
that are regular at every place of $K(C)$ over $K$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_boundedness_conjecture_for_rational_points)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [CHM1997] L. Caporaso, J. Harris, B. Mazur, *Uniformity of rational points*,
  J. Amer. Math. Soc. 10 (1997), 1–35.
* [DGH2021] V. Dimitrov, Z. Gao, P. Habegger, *Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves*,
  Ann. of Math. 194 (2021), 237–298. [arXiv:2001.10276](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.10276)
-/
namespace UniformBoundednessConjectureForRationalPoints
open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits
universe u
section FunctionField

blocks.command_arg: (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
blocks.text: variable (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]

blocks.code:
noncomputable def regularDifferentials : Submodule K Ω[L⁄K] :=
  ⨅ (A : Subalgebra K L) (_ : ∀ x : L, x ∈ A ∨ x⁻¹ ∈ A),
    (LinearMap.range (KaehlerDifferential.map K K A L)).restrictScalars K
blocks.docstring:
The `K`-vector space of Kähler differentials of `L` over `K` that are regular at every place of
`L` over `K`.

A `K`-subalgebra `A` of `L` such that `x ∈ A` or `x⁻¹ ∈ A` for every `x : L` is a valuation
subring of `L` containing `K`. When `L = K(C)` is the function field of a smooth projective
curve `C` over `K`, the proper such subalgebras are exactly the local rings `𝒪_{C, P}` at the
closed points `P` of `C` (and `A = L` imposes no condition). A differential `ω ∈ Ω[L⁄K]` is
regular at `P` when it lies in the image of `Ω[𝒪_{C, P}⁄K] → Ω[K(C)⁄K]`. Hence this space is
$H^0(C, \Omega^1_{C/K})$, the space of global sections of the sheaf of differentials.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `KaehlerDifferential` (Ω[L⁄K]) and `KaehlerDifferential.map` (used); `ValuationSubring` (not used directly because it carries no `Algebra K` instance, so `Subalgebra K L` with the valuation condition `x ∈ A ∨ x⁻¹ ∈ A` is used instead); `Sheaf.H` (Ext-based sheaf cohomology) for H^1(C, O_C), rejected because Mathlib provides no K-linear structure on the structure sheaf/its cohomology.
justification.name: UniformBoundednessConjectureForRationalPoints.regularDifferentials
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no divisors, no sheaf of differentials on schemes with computable global sections, and no genus. The space of Kähler differentials of L/K regular at every place (every valuation subring of L containing K) is H^0(C, Ω^1_{C/K}) when L = K(C) for a smooth projective curve C, and is expressible with `KaehlerDifferential.map`, `Subalgebra` and `Submodule.restrictScalars`.

blocks.name: regularDifferentials
blocks.text:
/--
The `K`-vector space of Kähler differentials of `L` over `K` that are regular at every place of
`L` over `K`.

A `K`-subalgebra `A` of `L` such that `x ∈ A` or `x⁻¹ ∈ A` for every `x : L` is a valuation
subring of `L` containing `K`. When `L = K(C)` is the function field of a smooth projective
curve `C` over `K`, the proper such subalgebras are exactly the local rings `𝒪_{C, P}` at the
closed points `P` of `C` (and `A = L` imposes no condition). A differential `ω ∈ Ω[L⁄K]` is

-/
noncomputable def regularDifferentials : Submodule K Ω[L⁄K] :=
  ⨅ (A : Subalgebra K L) (_ : ∀ x : L, x ∈ A ∨ x⁻¹ ∈ A),
    (LinearMap.range (KaehlerDifferential.map K K A L)).restrictScalars K

blocks.code: noncomputable def functionFieldGenus : ℕ := Module.finrank K (regularDifferentials K L)
blocks.docstring:
The genus of the function field `L` over `K`: the `K`-dimension of the space of differentials
of `L/K` that are regular at every place. For `L = K(C)` the function field of a smooth
projective geometrically irreducible curve `C` over `K` this is
$\dim_K H^0(C, \Omega^1_{C/K})$, the genus of `C`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib; `FunctionField` in Mathlib.NumberTheory.FunctionField only concerns finite extensions of Fq(t) and has no genus.
justification.name: UniformBoundednessConjectureForRationalPoints.functionFieldGenus
justification.why_needed: `Module.finrank K` of `regularDifferentials K L`: the genus of the function field L/K (= dim_K H^0(C, Ω) for the corresponding smooth projective curve). No notion of genus exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

blocks.name: functionFieldGenus
blocks.text:
/--
The genus of the function field `L` over `K`: the `K`-dimension of the space of differentials
of `L/K` that are regular at every place. For `L = K(C)` the function field of a smooth
projective geometrically irreducible curve `C` over `K` this is
$\dim_K H^0(C, \Omega^1_{C/K})$, the genus of `C`.
-/
noncomputable def functionFieldGenus : ℕ := Module.finrank K (regularDifferentials K L)
end FunctionField
section Curve

blocks.command_arg: (K : Type u) [Field K] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of K))
blocks.text: variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of K))

blocks.code: def rationalPoints : Set (Spec (.of K) ⟶ C) := {s | (s ≫ f) = 𝟙 _}
blocks.docstring:
The set of `K`-rational points of a `K`-scheme `C` with structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K`:

justification.name: UniformBoundednessConjectureForRationalPoints.rationalPoints
justification.why_needed: The set C(K) of K-rational points of a K-scheme, i.e. sections of the structure morphism `Spec K ⟶ C`. Mathlib has no definition of rational points of a scheme over a base.

blocks.name: rationalPoints
blocks.text:
/--
The set of `K`-rational points of a `K`-scheme `C` with structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K`:
the sections of `f`, that is, the `K`-morphisms `Spec K ⟶ C`.
-/
def rationalPoints : Set (Spec (.of K) ⟶ C) := {s | (s ≫ f) = 𝟙 _}

blocks.code:
def IsGeometricallyIrreducible : Prop :=
  IrreducibleSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))
blocks.docstring:
A `K`-scheme `C` with structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K` is geometrically irreducible if its
base change to an algebraic closure of `K` is irreducible.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IrreducibleSpace` and `Limits.pullback` (used to build it); `Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced`-style ring-level notions exist only for reducedness, not irreducibility.
justification.name: UniformBoundednessConjectureForRationalPoints.IsGeometricallyIrreducible
justification.why_needed: Geometric irreducibility of a K-scheme (irreducibility of the base change to an algebraic closure) is part of the standard definition of 'curve over K' in the cited literature and is absent from Mathlib for schemes.

blocks.name: IsGeometricallyIrreducible
blocks.text:
/--
A `K`-scheme `C` with structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K` is geometrically irreducible if its
base change to an algebraic closure of `K` is irreducible.
-/
def IsGeometricallyIrreducible : Prop :=
  IrreducibleSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))

blocks.code:
noncomputable def genus [IsIntegral C] : ℕ :=
  haveI : Nonempty (⊤ : C.Opens) := ⟨⟨genericPoint C, trivial⟩⟩
  letI : Algebra K C.functionField :=
    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ C.germToFunctionField ⊤).hom.toAlgebra
  functionFieldGenus K C.functionField
blocks.docstring:
The genus of an integral `K`-scheme `C` with structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K`, defined as
the genus of its function field `K(C)`, with the `K`-algebra structure on `K(C)` induced by `f`.
When `C` is a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over `K`, this is
$\dim_K H^0(C, \Omega^1_{C/K})$, the genus of `C`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.functionField` (used); no genus/Euler characteristic/sheaf-cohomology dimension for schemes exists in Mathlib.
justification.name: UniformBoundednessConjectureForRationalPoints.genus
justification.why_needed: The genus of an integral K-scheme C with structure morphism f, as the genus of its function field `C.functionField` with the K-algebra structure induced by f. Needed to state 'curve of genus g'.

The genus of an integral `K`-scheme `C` with structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K`, defined as
the genus of its function field `K(C)`, with the `K`-algebra structure on `K(C)` induced by `f`.
When `C` is a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over `K`, this is
$\dim_K H^0(C, \Omega^1_{C/K})$, the genus of `C`.

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem uniform_boundedness_conjecture_for_rational_points :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [NumberField K] (g : ℕ), 2 ≤ g →
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsIntegral C] [IsProper f]
        [IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f], IsGeometricallyIrreducible K f → genus K f = g →
        (rationalPoints K f).encard ≤ N := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points.**

Do algebraic curves of genus $g \geq 2$ over number fields $K$ have at most some bounded number
$N(K, g)$ of $K$-rational points?

That is, is it true that for every number field $K$ and every integer $g \geq 2$ there is a
number $N(K, g)$, depending only on $K$ and $g$, such that every smooth projective geometrically
irreducible curve $C$ over $K$ of genus $g$ satisfies $\#C(K) \leq N(K, g)$?

Here a curve is a scheme `C` over `Spec K` that is proper and smooth of relative dimension `1`
(hence projective) and geometrically irreducible. The hypothesis `IsIntegral C` is implied by
these (smooth over a field gives reduced, geometrically irreducible gives irreducible) and is
only needed to speak about the function field of `C`. By Faltings' theorem, each individual
$C(K)$ is finite; the conjecture asks for a bound that is uniform in $C$. The points are counted
with `Set.encard`, so the bound $\#C(K) \leq N$ also asserts that $C(K)$ is finite.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question whose positive answer is the Prop: for every number field K and every integer g ≥ 2 there exists N(K,g) such that every smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve C over K of genus g has #C(K) ≤ N(K,g); quantifier order matters (N depends only on K and g, not on C), 'algebraic curve' should be read as smooth/projective/geometrically irreducible per the cited literature (Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger intro), and the article's Caporaso–Harris–Mazur conditional result and Mazur's conjecture B (rank-dependent bound N(K,g,r), now a theorem) are background only and not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: c05 states the positive answer with the correct quantifier order (∀ K number field, ∀ g ≥ 2, ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ curve C/K) and models 'algebraic curve' scheme-theoretically as C : Scheme with f : C ⟶ Spec K, [IsProper f] (proper curve over a field ⇒ projective), [IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f], geometrically irreducible (base change to AlgebraicClosure K is irreducible), so together smooth projective geometrically integral curve. Genus is defined as dim_K of the Kähler differentials of K(C)/K lying in the image of Ω[A⁄K] for every valuation subring A ⊇ K of K(C); for a smooth proper geometrically integral curve these A are exactly the local rings at closed points (plus A = K(C)), and the intersection of the stalks of the locally free sheaf Ω^1_{C/K} inside the generic stalk is H^0(C, Ω^1), whose dimension is the genus. K-points are the sections of f, counted with Set.encard (so the bound also forces finiteness, no ncard junk). The redundant [IsIntegral C] instance is implied by the other hypotheses and only serves to make K(C) a field. Hypotheses are satisfiable (e.g. hyperelliptic curves), so not vacuous. I verified by #print that the repository's global asymptotics `≫` notation did not hijack the categorical composition in `rationalPoints` and `genus`. c03 (Riemann–Roch/Stichtenoth genus on the same scheme framework) is also faithful but has more moving parts; c06 (function-field reformulation) and c07 (embedded V(I) ⊆ ℙ^n with Hilbert polynomial + Jacobian criterion) are also mathematically faithful but further from the statement's 'algebraic curve'. Only the docstring was edited (one sentence about encard).

context: In arithmetic geometry, the uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points asserts that for a given number field $K$ and a positive integer $g\geq 2$, there exists a number $N(K,g)$ depending only on $K$ and $g$ such that for any algebraic curve $C$ defined over $K$ having genus equal to $g$ has at most $N(K,g)$ $K$ -rational points. This is a refinement of Faltings' theorem, which asserts that the set of $K$ -rational points $C(K)$ is necessarily finite.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single slot matches the source; the notes' reading of 'algebraic curve' as smooth/projective/geometrically irreducible and the exclusion of the CHM result and Mazur's conjecture B are followed.

/-!
# Uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points

Do algebraic curves of genus $g \geq 2$ over number fields $K$ have at most some bounded
number $N(K, g)$ of $K$-rational points?

geometrically irreducible variety of dimension $1$ over $K$. We model it as a scheme `C` with a

*References:*
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_boundedness_conjecture_for_rational_points)

universe u

section FunctionField

variable (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]

/--

noncomputable def regularDifferentials : Submodule K Ω[L⁄K] :=

of `L/K` that are regular at every place. For `L = K(C)` the function field of a smooth

end FunctionField

section Curve

variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of K))

/--
The set of `K`-rational points of a `K`-scheme `C` with structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K`:
the sections of `f`, that is, the `K`-morphisms `Spec K ⟶ C`.
-/
def rationalPoints : Set (Spec (.of K) ⟶ C) := {s | (s ≫ f) = 𝟙 _}

/--
A `K`-scheme `C` with structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K` is geometrically irreducible if its
base change to an algebraic closure of `K` is irreducible.
-/
def IsGeometricallyIrreducible : Prop :=
  IrreducibleSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))

/--
The genus of an integral `K`-scheme `C` with structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K`, defined as
the genus of its function field `K(C)`, with the `K`-algebra structure on `K(C)` induced by `f`.
When `C` is a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over `K`, this is

noncomputable def genus [IsIntegral C] : ℕ :=

@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem rationalPoints_id : rationalPoints K (𝟙 (Spec (.of K))) = {𝟙 _} := by
  ext s
  simp [rationalPoints]

end Curve

/--
**Uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points.**

Do algebraic curves of genus $g \geq 2$ over number fields $K$ have at most some bounded number
$N(K, g)$ of $K$-rational points?

That is, is it true that for every number field $K$ and every integer $g \geq 2$ there is a
number $N(K, g)$, depending only on $K$ and $g$, such that every smooth projective geometrically
irreducible curve $C$ over $K$ of genus $g$ satisfies $\#C(K) \leq N(K, g)$?

Here a curve is a scheme `C` over `Spec K` that is proper and smooth of relative dimension `1`
(hence projective) and geometrically irreducible. The hypothesis `IsIntegral C` is implied by
these (smooth over a field gives reduced, geometrically irreducible gives irreducible) and is
only needed to speak about the function field of `C`. By Faltings' theorem, each individual
$C(K)$ is finite; the conjecture asks for a bound that is uniform in $C$. The points are counted
with `Set.encard`, so the bound $\#C(K) \leq N$ also asserts that $C(K)$ is finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem uniform_boundedness_conjecture_for_rational_points :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [NumberField K] (g : ℕ), 2 ≤ g →
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsIntegral C] [IsProper f]
        [IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f], IsGeometricallyIrreducible K f → genus K f = g →
        (rationalPoints K f).encard ≤ N := by
  sorry

end UniformBoundednessConjectureForRationalPoints

items: 'Algebraic curve over K' is read, per the notes and Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger's intro, as a smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible variety of dimension 1 over K. Modelled as a scheme `C : Scheme.{u}` with structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec (.of K)` satisfying `IsProper f` and `IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f` (proper curves over a field are projective), plus geometric irreducibility.

The question is phrased as a yes/no question in the source, so the CONTRIBUTING idiom `answer(sorry) ↔ P` is used, with P the positive statement (existence of the uniform bound N(K,g)). All quantifiers (K, g, N, C) are after `answer(sorry)`; the statement is universe-polymorphic in `u` with `K : Type u`, `C : Scheme.{u}`.

Genus: defined as dim_K H^0(C, Ω^1_{C/K}) computed inside the function field K(C): `regularDifferentials K L` is the K-subspace of Kähler differentials `Ω[L⁄K]` lying in the image of `Ω[A⁄K] → Ω[L⁄K]` for every K-subalgebra A of L with `∀ x, x ∈ A ∨ x⁻¹ ∈ A` (i.e. every valuation subring of L containing K; for L = K(C) with C smooth proper these are exactly the local rings at closed points, and A = L imposes no condition). `functionFieldGenus K L := Module.finrank K (regularDifferentials K L)`, and `genus K f := functionFieldGenus K C.functionField` with the K-algebra structure on K(C) induced by f via `ΓSpecIso`, `f.appTop` and `germToFunctionField ⊤`. For a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve this equals the genus (h^0(Ω) = h^1(O) = g), so the hypothesis `genus K f = g` with g ≥ 2 is satisfiable (e.g. y² = x⁵ + 1), and the statement is not vacuous. A reviewer should check this identification of H^0(C, Ω) with differentials of K(C) regular at all places.

The theorem carries the extra instance hypothesis `[IsIntegral C]`, needed only so that `C.functionField` is a field (to talk about valuation subrings). It is implied by the other hypotheses (smooth over a field ⇒ reduced; geometrically irreducible ⇒ irreducible), so it does not restrict the class of curves; this is explained in the docstring.

Geometric irreducibility is defined as `IrreducibleSpace` of the underlying space of the scheme pullback of f along `Spec (AlgebraicClosure K) ⟶ Spec K` (irreducibility of the base change to an algebraic closure; independent of the chosen closure).

K-rational points are the sections of f: `rationalPoints K f := {s : Spec (.of K) ⟶ C | s ≫ f = 𝟙 _}`. The bound uses `Set.encard ≤ (N : ℕ∞)` rather than `ncard`, so an infinite set of points would violate the bound instead of trivially satisfying it (Faltings' finiteness is not assumed). Note the repository globally overloads `≫` for asymptotics, so the categorical composite is parenthesised as `(s ≫ f) = 𝟙 _`; `#print` confirms it elaborates to the categorical composition.

The Caporaso–Harris–Mazur conditional result and Mazur's conjecture B (rank-dependent bound, now the Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger theorem) are background only and are not formalized, per the decomposition notes. A small proven `@[category test]` (`rationalPoints_id`: the only K-point of Spec K is the identity) sanity-checks the `rationalPoints` definition.
